card.name: Linking words in old historical prose
card.fires_on: Small grammar words (to, now, there, it, I, remain, holds) and mid-word pieces in old-fashioned historical or political prose, such as local histories, oil-field reports and socialist essays.

modes.label: Verbs and links in claims
modes.description: Short verbs or linking words in the middle of a clause in old political or scientific writing.
modes.example: What De Leon said in his memorable New Bedford address forty-three years ago<< holds>> good today — in some respects even more

modes.label: Local history small words
modes.description: Small words like to, there, it in county or industry histories.

modes.label: Inside place or trade words
modes.description: Partway through words like hamlets or grist-mills.
modes.example: The village of Atlas, from point of location, is one of the most attractive of the ham<<lets>> of the county

card.plain: It fires on small connecting words in old-style historical writing, not on medical text.
